title: Assemble a food processor so it can run: lock the bowl on the base, lock the lid, close the interlock
instruction: Assemble the food processor so it is ready to run: lock the work bowl onto the base and the lid onto the bowl, then let go of both.
context: Food processors are in most kitchens and come apart for washing after every use, so whoever uses one assembles it every time: the bowl onto the motor base, turned until it locks, then the lid, turned until it locks. The motor runs only when the lid's tab, turned fully home, pushes the safety rod in the bowl's handle down onto the base's switch, so a half-turned bowl or lid leaves the processor dead. The skill is physical: lowering an 18 cm bowl, held by its handle and rim, over a drive shaft so its hidden lugs drop between the base's ledges, turning it against a detent with both hands, then seating the lid over the rim and turning it home by its feed tube against a detent and the interlock spring.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top; angles are seen from above, counter-clockwise from +x. Motor base (white ABS housing 20 x 17 x 9.5 cm, 4.2 kg, rubber feet), centred on its drive shaft at (0.415, 0); on top a grey coupling boss 110 mm across and 20 mm tall (top 11.5 cm up) with three ledges round its top edge (each 25 degrees long, 9 mm thick, reaching 12 mm out from the boss, at 18.5-43.5, 138.5-163.5 and 258.5-283.5 degrees, a stop post at each ledge's clockwise end, a 6 mm notch at 30 degrees in the first); a steel drive-shaft hub 25 mm across standing 50 mm above the boss with a 10 mm conical tip. Work bowl (clear polycarbonate, 9 cup, 0.55 kg): 180 mm outside diameter, 3 mm wall, 125 mm tall; a centre tube of 29 mm bore, 105 mm tall; a 148 mm foot skirt 17.5 mm deep with three 22-degree lugs inside it (inner faces 57.5 mm from the axis); a grey handle (30 x 24 mm upright bar, 13 cm from the axis, on the bowl's front right when locked) and, down its inside, a red 6 mm switch rod standing 9 mm proud of the handle's top, sprung up (1.0 N, 1.4 N when pressed 7 mm); four ledges round the outside of the rim, 6.5-15.5 mm below its top, each with a stop and an 8 mm lead-in ramp; a sprung detent plunger (3 N) in one foot lug and one rim ledge. It stands upright on its foot at (0.20, 0), handle on its right (at 270 degrees; turned 28 degrees counter-clockwise of locked). Lid (clear polycarbonate, 0.25 kg): 212 mm across, a 24 mm skirt with four 22-degree lugs inside it; a feed tube 40 x 70 mm outside, 10 cm tall, centred 58 mm off the axis; a grey interlock tab sticking out of the skirt (flat underside, 30-degree ramp on its clockwise side). It stands on its skirt at (0.27, -0.30), feed tube toward the robot's right and back (at 298 degrees about its centre; tab at 270 degrees). Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the bowl or the lid falls off the table, either is forced more than 3 degrees past its stops while seated, or the switch rod or a detent plunger is forced 2 mm past its end; lifting, tilting, setting down or dropping a part on the table is allowed. Otherwise the stage at the end: 0.25 the bowl seated over the shaft (axis within 4 mm, tilted under 3 degrees, floor from 2 mm below to 3 mm above the boss's top); 0.5 the bowl locked (seated and turned to within 3 degrees of its stops: every lug wholly under its ledge); 0.75 the bowl locked and the lid seated on its rim (axis within 4 mm, tilt under 3 degrees, from 2 mm below to 3 mm above the rim). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): the bowl locked with its handle over the base's switch, the lid locked within 3 degrees of its stops, the switch rod pushed down at least 5 mm, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the bowl and the lid, both still (under 1 cm/s). Holding the lid in place scores 0.75. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Turn the lid counter-clockwise and lift it off; stand it on its skirt at its mark, feed tube to the back right. Turn the bowl counter-clockwise, lift it off the shaft and stand it on its foot at its mark, handle on its right. Use the processor unplugged, with no blade fitted.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Round walls, skirts and rings are flat panels; boss and shaft are cylinders. The bowl is an articulation with three sprung slider links: switch rod 1 N preload, 60 N/m (light: a stiffer one lifted the lid in its lug play); two detent plungers 3 N, 300 N/m, with 45-degree tips. Spring forces are estimates, not measured on a product. The base is fixed. The bowl's taper, the blade, discs and food pusher are left out. Friction 0.4.
